metaTitle: Restaurant Marketing in Coral Gables, FL | Button Up Media
metaDescription: Restaurant marketing in Coral Gables: polished photo and video, Google Maps and reviews, bilingual content and ads from a Miami team that shoots on site.
answer: Button Up Media is a Miami restaurant marketing agency that helps Coral Gables restaurants fill lunches and dinners with polished content, Google visibility and bilingual ads.
heroSub: In the Gables, your storefront stays quiet by design. Your photos, reviews and Google listing have to do the talking.

paragraphsHtml: Coral Gables was planned as “The City Beautiful,” and it still runs that way. A Board of Architects reviews how buildings look and signage stays understated, so you cannot out-shout the restaurant next door with a bigger sign. Most new guests find you online first and walk in second.

You are also serving several crowds on the same day: client lunches from the Ponce de Leon Boulevard office corridor, residents planning a date night or a celebration, and visitors to the Biltmore and the University of Miami who do not know the area. Each group searches differently, and many of your guests search, read reviews and decide in Spanish.

Expectations are high. Diners here compare you with rooms that have built their reputations over decades, so a blurry phone photo or a listing full of old reviews quietly puts you in a lower tier, even when your kitchen is not.

needs.h2: What a Coral Gables restaurant needs most

items.title: Photos that look as good as the room
items.body: Your images carry your brand here, because your exterior cannot. Food, dining room and service shot professionally and kept consistent across Google, Instagram and your website, so guests see the same restaurant everywhere they look.

items.title: A complete Google listing with fresh reviews
items.body: Correct categories, current hours and menu, a working reservation link, and recent reviews answered in the guest's language. For an upscale room, a page of recent, detailed reviews often settles the choice.

items.title: Fast booking for the lunch crowd
items.body: Office lunches get planned quickly. A clear menu online and a reservation or private-room inquiry that takes seconds on a phone wins the table before a competitor does.

items.title: English and Spanish, written like a local
items.body: A feed and listing that only speak English miss a large part of your own neighborhood. Both languages should read like they were written here, not translated at the end.
A coffee shop and art space in nearby Pinecrest, known for its creative lattes. Its content, including a standout butter coffee video, has drawn 40M organic views.

plan.h2: What we would do for a Coral Gables restaurant

items.title: Polished content on a steady schedule
items.bodyHtml: We shoot your food, room and service on site, then keep Instagram and TikTok current with posts that look like the experience you built. That is how our restaurant social media and content service runs.

items.title: Google listing and reviews
items.bodyHtml: We fix your Google Business Profile, keep it active and reply to reviews in English and Spanish, so you show up for searches like “dinner in Coral Gables.” It is the core of our restaurant SEO and Google Business Profile work.

items.title: A website as refined as the room
items.bodyHtml: A custom-coded, bilingual, mobile-first site with your menu, your story and reservations built in, so a resident or a visitor can book in a few taps. See our restaurant website design work.

items.title: Ads for lunches, celebrations and private events
items.bodyHtml: Google Ads reach people searching nearby right now, and Meta ads reach residents planning an anniversary or an event, all tracked to calls, reservations and inquiries. For a landmark waterfront restaurant, a private-events search campaign returned 72:1 on ad spend from May to December 2025. See how our restaurant Google and Meta ads work.

shoots.h2: How shoots work in Coral Gables
shoots.body: We come to your restaurant and shoot there, scheduled around lunch and dinner so service runs normally. Plated dishes are usually captured before doors open, and the dining room when the light suits it. The same in-house team that plans your content shoots it, and one shoot typically gives us 4 to 6 weeks of content across your platforms. Planning starts with a strategy call hosted by Juan Hernandez, our founder, so the shoot covers what your guests actually care about.

pricing.bodyHtml: Most restaurants invest $1,500 to $5,000 per month for a coordinated program across content, Google and ads. If your site needs work first, a custom build is a one-time $1,500 (Website Build) or $2,000 (Integrated Website Build, which adds POS menu sync, reservations and ordering). Ad management carries no long-term contract. To see how you compare with nearby restaurants before you spend anything, run the free Social Media & Website Grader.

faqs.q: Do you work with restaurants in Coral Gables?
faqs.a: Yes. We work with restaurants, bars and cafes across Miami-Dade. Our work nearby includes Brewing Buddha in Pinecrest, featured in our case studies.

faqs.q: Can you shoot without disrupting lunch service?
faqs.a: Yes. Shoots are scheduled around your service, and most food and drink content is captured before doors open.

faqs.q: Can you reply to reviews in Spanish?
faqs.a: Yes. Our team is bilingual, so review replies, captions, ads and your website can run in English, Spanish or both.

faqs.q: Can you help us book more private events?
faqs.a: Yes. We run Google Ads built around private-event inquiries and reservations, with conversion tracking so you can see what each inquiry costs.
